item.title: A Negative-U Double Quantum Dot in a LaAlO3/SrTiO3 Membrane on Silicon
item.description:
Pay dirt new result — Realized a double quantum dot with attractive on-site interaction in an oxide membrane on silicon. Transport shows paired-electron ground states with on-site interaction U = -35μeV, interdot tunnel coupling t = 80μeV, and interdot interaction W=0 meV.

Grade 0.444 · 2.1σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Giulia Meucci, Thies Jansen, Pinelopi O. Konstantinopoulou, Dags Olvsteins, Damon J. Carrad, Carina Babu Maliakkal, Jordi Arbiol, Nicolas Bergeal, Manuel Bibes, Roberta Citro, Emiliano Di Gennaro, Alexei Kalaboukhov, Nicola Manca, Carmine A. Perroni, Marco Salluzzo, Paweł Wójcik, Felix Trier, Nini Pryds, Fabio Miletto Granozio, Alessia Sambri, Thomas S. Jespersen

Figure

Differential conductance G versus gate voltages VG1 and VG2 at B∥=0 T and 3 T, comparing experiment to attractive two-site Hubbard simulations. Honeycomb charge stability diagrams show paired transitions at B∥=0 T and splitting into single-electron regimes above the pairing field.

Asks

Can local electrostatic gates control the correlated electronic states of transferred oxide membranes on silicon at the scale required for mesoscopic quantum devices?

But

Tbase=20 mK, B⟂=200 mT; anticrossing gap Δ02−11 is below experimental resolution.

Tools

spalled LaAlO₃/SrTiO₃ micro-membranes · electron-beam lithography defined local top-gates · dilution refrigerator transport spectroscopy · two-orbital Anderson model in QmeQ

Abstract

The development of freestanding oxide membranes creates new opportunities to integrate oxide functionalities with silicon technology. A central question is whether local gates can control the correlated electronic states of transferred membranes at the scale required for hybrid mesoscopic quantum devices. Here, we demonstrate local electrostatic control of freestanding LaAlO3/SrTiO3 (LAO/STO) membranes transferred onto silicon. In a dual-gated constriction in the interfacial electron system, we observe an oxide-based double quantum dot (DQD) in the regime of attractive on-site interactions (U < 0). Low-temperature transport reveals the characteristic honeycomb charge stability diagram, and spectroscopy identifies a paired-electron ground state at low magnetic fields, with odd-occupancy states becoming accessible above the pairing field. The observed transport spectra are reproduced by simulations within an attractive two site Hubbard model, and we extract the relevant DQD parameters, including intradot and interdot interactions, interdot tunnel coupling, and spin-orbit-assisted tunnel coupling. These findings establish oxide membranes as hosts for DQDs and extend coupled quantum dot systems into the regime of attractive on-site interactions.

item.title: Physical Learning for Autonomous Tuning of Spin Qubits in Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dots
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Multiplexed gradient descent on an FPGA local controller continuously tracks drift up to 0.3 mV/s and recovers from discrete jumps up to 1 mV in 0.7 s (330 iterations), holding within a 134 μV tolerance without prior knowledge of the cross-capacitance matrix.

Grade 0.428 · 1.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Leonardo Gaytan, Bradley Lloyd, Paul Kliewer, Chandler Wilburn, Lincoln D. Carr, Adam McCaughan, Sonia Buckley, Meenakshi Singh

Asks

How can electrostatically defined quantum dots be autonomously stabilized at target idling and pulsing points without repeating full charge-stability diagram scans or relying on model-dependent feedback loops?

Before

Continuous stabilization required periodic 2D scans taking seconds followed by neural-network and Hough transform inference, or monotonic single-peak PID loops that diverge under cross-capacitance.

But

Quantum dot and charge noise simulated rather than physically measured on-chip. Pulsing point assumes both virtual-gate directions are constrained, which requires two SETs in physical implementation.

Tools

multiplexed gradient descent (MGD) · simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation (SPSA) · FPGA-in-the-loop controller · simulated double quantum dot and SET sensor

Abstract

Tuning electrostatically defined quantum dots remains a primary bottleneck in the scalability of semiconductor spin qubits. While existing solutions rely on machine learning algorithms, these approaches require global information, introduce latency bottlenecks, and tax the limited cooling power available at cryogenic stages. Here, we demonstrate an FPGA-in-the-loop learning paradigm that bypasses digital computing overhead by utilizing multiplexed gradient descent (MGD) for tuning. Implemented on an FPGA and an emulated quantum dot device, our system autonomously tracks environmental drift, dynamically recovers from discrete charge jumps, and maintains steady-state stabilization in low signal-to-noise ratio regimes, without prior knowledge of the device's cross-capacitance matrix. The system also navigates the charge-stability landscape to stabilize the quantum dot around optimal operating points. These results demonstrate a ``compute-in-place'' platform, with a logic and power footprint suited to future cryo-CMOS integration, that provides autonomous stabilization of quantum dots at desired operating points, creating an auto-tuning system for spin qubits that is resilient to electrostatic drifts, changing noise profiles, and two-level fluctuations.

item.title: Thermo-electric Response Bound on Fluctuations in Coherent Transport
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Zero-frequency current noise is lower-bounded by S≥∑NhkBTN[(∂J/∂TN)2/(ℓ0kB2)+(∂J/∂μN−wNQJNC/e)2], evaluated purely via differential thermoelectric and electrical response coefficients.

Grade 0.426 · 1.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “Charge-insensitive qubit design derived from the Cooper pair box” · Gianmichele Blasi, Rosa López, Mykhailo Moskalets, Sungguen Ryu

Figure

Tightness of the thermo-electric response bound for charge current plotted as a function of electrical bias V across a finite-gap normal-superconductor junction at fixed temperature T.

Asks

How can current fluctuations in coherent mesoscopic transport under static or periodic driving be bounded directly by experimentally accessible response coefficients without relying on entropy production or dynamical activity?

But

Coherent noninteracting transport with noninteracting leads; cannot capture partition-induced off-diagonal noise terms.

Tools

Floquet-Nambu scattering formalism · Cramér-Rao inequality · Cauchy-Schwarz inequality on inner-product space of scattering matrices

Abstract

We establish an accessible lower bound on current noise in coherent electron transport, expressed in terms of responses to reservoir temperatures and chemical potentials. Derived within the Floquet-Nambu scattering formalism using a Cramér-Rao-type inequality, it holds for arbitrary linear combinations of charge and heat currents in normal terminals, including those of hybrid superconducting systems, under static or periodic driving. The bound is tight in experimentally relevant regimes, notably in quantum point contacts with static or oscillating voltages and normal-superconductor junctions, often providing stronger constraints than thermodynamic uncertainty relations. It can be evaluated via experimentally accessible response coefficients, without inferring entropy production or dynamical activity, and provides useful constraints on the precision of nanoscale thermal and quantum devices.

item.title: Minimal chiral p-wave superconductor
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Square array of quantum dots coupled via proximitized Andreev dots achieves zero edge-state decay length along crystal axes at μ=−2Δ0 and t=Δ0, yielding chiral transport in 3×3 and an isolated vortex Majorana zero mode with sub-percent splitting in 5×5 arrays.

Grade 0.415 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Fabian Hassler, Michael Wimmer

Figure

Energy spectra and conductance for a 5×5 quantum-dot array. Panels show the emergence of a near-zero-energy vortex core Majorana mode upon adding flux, distinct from boundary-localized edge states, and its signature in local tunneling conductance.

Asks

Can a chiral p-wave superconductor with well-separated Majorana modes and chiral edge states be assembled from quantum dots in two dimensions?

But

Nearest-neighbor tight-binding coupling; requires Zeeman splitting larger than cotunneling and crossed Andreev reflection rates; zero-temperature linear-response calculations.

Tools

tight-binding Bogoliubov-de Gennes model · Rashba spin-orbit coupling · crossed Andreev reflection · Kwant scattering matrix simulations

Abstract

Chiral p-wave superconductors are among the most intriguing topological phases: their vortices bind Majorana zero modes and their edges carry chiral Majorana modes, yet no material has been unambiguously identified as one. Here, we carry the bottom-up approach of Kitaev chains to two dimensions, proposing a minimal chiral p-wave superconductor from a square array of quantum dots coupled via Andreev dots. Rashba spin-orbit coupling in the tunnel barriers provides the p-wave winding, and a Zeeman field renders the dots spinless. At a sweet spot, the edge states are confined to the outermost row, so that a chiral thermal conductance and a vortex-bound Majorana zero mode with sub-percent splitting emerge already in 3×3 and 5×5 arrays. Our setup is realizable with existing InAs and Ge quantum-dot arrays.
